objective: Which hypothesis most reduces risk of misleading or unsafe structural engineering output?
rationale: Under the safety objective, blocking final-approval language when verified AISC source is missing (A) reduces the misleading-output risk more directly than exposing pass/warn/block decisions (B). Confidence is moderate-high but not certain: the effect size is not yet measured.
facts_used: ev-international-policy-aisc-001: AISC/ASCE experimental mode must not invent verified section properties or claim final compliance without verified input or source.
ev-agent-ecosystem-guardrail-001: the agent ecosystem strategy recommends guardrails that block final-approval language, invented AISC values and mixed standards.
inferences: Blocking final-approval language at output time acts on the professional-review boundary itself, whereas a read-only decision dashboard improves observability of existing decisions without preventing the unsafe claim.
Both improve safety, but A addresses the failure mode (false confidence) more directly than B.
safety_concerns: Must not over-block legitimate demand-only or diagnostic output; the blocking wording itself requires professional review.
